blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Three-dimensional spatial transcriptomics (3D ST) enables the analysis of gene-expression patterns across tissue depths. However, 3D ST measurements are acquired from discrete 2D tissue sections, which are often sparsely sampled due to high acquisition costs. To address this limitation, we propose a histology-informed multi-task implicit neural representation (HIM-INR) for continuous 3D gene-expression reconstruction from sparse ST observations. HIM-INR jointly reconstructs gene-expression profiles and histological representations using an INR with a shared backbone, leveraging densely sampled histological images as auxiliary spatial supervision. Once trained, HIM-INR predicts gene expression at arbitrary 3D coordinates without requiring histological images. Experiments on two 3D ST datasets demonstrate improved reconstruction over existing methods, particularly as the number of missing ST sections increases.
blocks.zh: 三维空间转录相学(3D ST)可以分析跨组织深度的基因表达模式. 然而,从离散的2D组织部分获得3D ST测量,由于获取成本高,这些部分往往很少采样. 为了解决这一局限性,我们提议一种基于神学的多任务隐含神经表达(HIM-INR),用于从稀少的ST观测中持续地进行3D基因表达重建. HIM-INR联合重建了基因表达剖面图和以共享骨干为主的INR来进行组织表达,利用了密集的样本的神学图像作为辅助空间监督. 接受过训练后,HIM-INR在任意3D坐标时预测基因表达,而不需要组织图像. 对两个3D ST数据集的实验表明,重建工作比现有方法有所改善,特别是随着所缺的ST段数量增加.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Three-dimensional spatial transcriptomics (3D ST) [ 1 ] has emerged as a promising approach for investigating the spatial organization of gene expression within tissues.
Building on conventional 2D ST [ 2 ] ,
which measures gene expression in individual tissue sections,
3D ST enables the characterization of molecular interactions
across tissue depths and the spatial extent and connectivity
of pathological regions. Such capabilities offer new opportunities to investigate cell-to-cell communication across sections, characterize tumor invasion and inflammatory infiltration, and reveal spatial relationships between tissue architecture and molecular states that cannot be fully captured by individual 2D sections [ 1 , 3 ] .

blocks.en:
Despite the potential of 3D ST, gene expression is measured

from serial tissue sections into a common spatial coordinate
system to reconstruct tissue structures along the depth
axis [ 4 , 5 ] .
However, gene-expression information remains restricted
to the observed sections, leaving the continuous distribution
of gene expression between them unresolved.

blocks.en:
These limitations motivate the reconstruction of a continuous
3D gene-expression field from sparsely and discretely observed ST sections.
However, this task remains challenging.
While gene expression can vary substantially with changes in tissue structure across sections, no direct information on gene expression is available between sparsely sampled ST sections.
Consequently, not only conventional neighborhood-based interpolation
methods but also deep learning-based approaches [ 6 , 7 ] that model nonlinear relationships between spatial positions
and gene expression face difficulties in accurately reconstructing
gene expression in unobserved regions.

blocks.en:
To address this challenge, our key idea is to leverage
histological images, which provide detailed morphological
information about tissue structure.
Gene-expression patterns are known to be associated with tissue structure and morphology [ 8 , 9 ] .
Moreover, histological images are commonly acquired alongside ST measurements and are often available from more densely sampled tissue sections due to their substantially lower acquisition cost [ 10 ] .
Thus, histological information can provide valuable cues
about variations in tissue morphology, even at locations
where ST measurements are unavailable, potentially facilitating
continuous 3D gene-expression reconstruction.

此外,组织图象通常与ST测量同时获得,而且由于采集成本低得多,往往从更密集的样本组织部分获取[10]。

blocks.en:
In this study, we propose a histology-informed multi-task implicit neural representation
(HIM-INR) framework for reconstructing gene-expression profiles
at arbitrary 3D coordinates from sparsely sampled ST sections,
as illustrated in Fig. 1 .
We base our method on an INR model, which represents continuous
signals by learning a function that maps spatial coordinates
to corresponding signal values [ 11 ] .
Using the INR as a shared backbone, our framework jointly reconstructs
gene-expression profiles and histological representations extracted
using a pretrained pathology foundation model designed to capture
tissue morphology [ 12 ] .
By incorporating histological reconstruction as an auxiliary task,
the shared INR backbone receives additional spatial supervision
from densely sampled histological sections, even at locations
where ST measurements are unavailable.
This encourages the model to capture continuous variations in
tissue morphology and learn shared spatial representations
for gene-expression and histological reconstruction.
Importantly, inference requires only 3D coordinates, enabling
gene-expression reconstruction even at locations where neither
ST measurements nor histological images are available.

blocks.en:
We evaluate the proposed framework on two publicly available 3D ST datasets and compare it with conventional interpolation methods and INR-based reconstruction approaches.
Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing approaches under most evaluation settings, highlighting the effectiveness of incorporating histological information for reconstructing gene expression profiles at unobserved sections.
In particular, the benefits of histological supervision become more pronounced as the number of missing ST sections increases, highlighting its potential for reconstructing continuous gene expression fields from sparse observations.

实验结果表明,在大多数评价环境中,我们的方法优于现有方法,突出了将组织学信息纳入在未观察区重建基因表达剖面的有效性。
特别是,随着缺失的ST节数的增加,组织学监督的好处变得更加明显,突出了它从稀少的观测中重建连续基因表达领域的潜力.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
3D ST Reconstruction. Recent studies have explored 3D ST analysis by integrating transcriptomic measurements from serial tissue sections.
Most approaches focus on aligning consecutive sections to reconstruct their spatial organization [ 4 , 5 ] .
Although these methods enable the analysis of spatial relationships across observed sections, they do not reconstruct gene-expression patterns in unobserved regions between sections, limiting continuous 3D analysis.

多数方法侧重于调整连续各节,以重建其空间组织[4,5]。
虽然这些方法能够分析被观测到的各段之间的空间关系,但是它们并没有在各段之间的未观测区域重建基因表达模式,限制了连续的3D分析.

blocks.en:
Recent methods have addressed gene-expression reconstruction
between sparsely observed tissue sections.
STAGE [ 6 ] aligns the latent space of a
gene-expression autoencoder with spatial coordinates,

SINTER3D [ 7 ] uses an
INR [ 11 ] to predict gene expression
at unobserved 3D coordinates.
However, learning spatial continuity solely from
transcriptomic measurements remains challenging when
ST sections are sparsely sampled along the depth axis.
In contrast, we explore the potential of leveraging
more densely sampled histological images as auxiliary
supervision to encourage the INR to capture morphological
variations between observed ST sections.

blocks.en:
INR for ST Analysis. INR parameterizes continuous signals using neural networks that map spatial coordinates to signal values [ 11 ] .
Recent studies have applied INR to impute missing gene-expression values and reconstruct expression at unobserved locations in 2D ST [ 13 , 14 ] .
STINR [ 13 ] directly regresses gene-expression profiles from spatial coordinates, whereas SUICA [ 14 ] addresses high-dimensional expression reconstruction by learning a low-dimensional latent representation predicted using INR.
However, these methods primarily focus on reconstruction
within individual 2D tissue sections rather than continuous
modeling of gene expression in 3D space across aligned sections.

blocks.en: 3 Histology-Informed Multi-task INR
blocks.zh: 3 Histology-Informed 多任务 INR

blocks.en: 3.1 Overview
blocks.zh: 3.1 概览

blocks.en:
We propose HIM-INR to reconstruct gene expression at arbitrary 3D coordinates using sparsely observed ST sections and more densely sampled histological images.
As illustrated in Fig. 1 , HIM-INR consists of
two reconstruction branches for gene expression and histology
image features, sharing a SIREN-based INR backbone [ 11 ] .
Inspired by Zhu et al. [ 14 ] , we address the difficulty of modeling high-dimensional vectors with INR by learning spatial continuity in low-dimensional latent spaces for both modalities.
The predicted latent representations are then decoded into
gene-expression profiles and histology image features.
During training, the model is jointly optimized using reconstruction losses for both modalities.
Importantly, the histological-feature reconstruction branch is also trained on sections without ST measurements, encouraging the shared INR backbone to capture tissue structural information that guides gene-expression reconstruction in unobserved regions.

blocks.en: 3.2 Latent Representations of ST and Histology Features
blocks.zh: 3.2 晚期表现

blocks.en:
To enable the INR to learn spatial continuity in low-dimensional latent spaces rather than directly modeling high-dimensional observations, we employ autoencoders to obtain latent representations of both gene-expression profiles and histology image features.
We independently pretrain MLP-based autoencoders for each modality using a mean squared error (MSE) reconstruction loss, with latent dimensions d G d_{G} and d I d_{I} , respectively.
After pretraining, the encoders are frozen and used to extract latent representations 𝐳 i G ∈ ℝ d G \mathbf{z}_{i}^{G}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{G}} and 𝐳 i I ∈ ℝ d I \mathbf{z}_{i}^{I}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{I}} from the corresponding observations.
These representations serve as fixed targets for subsequent INR training.

blocks.en:
We jointly learn continuous representations of sparsely observed ST and densely sampled histological images through a shared INR backbone f f .
By incorporating image-only sections during training, the shared backbone captures spatial variations in tissue structure even at locations without ST observations, thereby guiding gene-expression reconstruction.

blocks.en: 4 Experiments
blocks.zh: 4 实验

blocks.en:
Datasets and Experimental Settings. Although histological images are commonly acquired alongside
ST measurements [ 17 ] ,
large-scale, publicly available 3D ST datasets with paired
histological images remain limited. We therefore select two datasets with relatively large numbers of sections, 3DST-RA [ 15 ] and HemiBrain [ 16 ] . To evaluate our method, we artificially withhold tissue sections to simulate missing observations.
blocks.zh:
数据集与实验设置. 虽然通常同时获得组织图象
ST测量 [17],
大型、可公开使用的配对的3D ST数据集
组织图象仍然有限。 因此,我们选择了两套数据,其中3DST-RA[15]和HemiBrain[16]段数量相对较多。 为了评估我们的方法,我们人为地扣留组织部分来模拟缺失的观测.

blocks.en:
3DST-RA contains paired ST measurements and histological images from serial synovial tissue sections of patients with rheumatoid arthritis.
We select the patient with the largest number of sections, consisting of seven consecutive sections numbered from 1 to 7. ST measurements are retained for Sections 1, 4, and 7. Among the remaining four sections, three are used as image-only observations, while one is completely withheld for evaluation. We repeat this evaluation four times, each time selecting a different section to be completely withheld.
blocks.zh:
3DST-RA包含对称的ST测量,以及来自风湿性关节炎患者的连环组织段的组织图像.
我们选择的病人的分科数量最多,由连续7个从1到7的分科组成. 第1、4和7节保留ST测量。 在其余的四节中,三节用作只观察图像,一节则完全不用于评价. 我们重复了4次评估,每次选择不同的部分,完全不作评价。

blocks.en: The HemiBrain dataset contains serial brain sections from three mice. We use two samples, HemiBrainA and HemiBrainB, containing 42 and 9 sections, respectively. We retain both ST measurements and histological images at every fourth section. Among the three intermediate sections, the first and third are used as image-only observations, while the second is withheld for evaluation.
blocks.zh: HemiBrain数据集包含三只小鼠的连环脑部分. 我们使用两个样本,即HemiBrainA和HemiBrainB,分别包含42节和9节. 我们保留了 ST 测量和组织图像 每第四节。 在三个中间部分中,第一组和第三组仅用作图像观测,而第二组则不予评价。

blocks.en: Prior to training and evaluation, adjacent tissue sections are aligned using XFeat-based feature matching [ 18 ] and RANSAC-based similarity transformations [ 19 ] . These transformations are sequentially composed to register all sections to a common coordinate system, with the middle section as the reference. Evaluation-section histological images are also used for registration to ensure accurate spatial correspondence between predicted and ground-truth gene-expression profiles, but are excluded from model training, inference, and performance evaluation.
blocks.zh: 在培训和评价之前,相邻的组织部分使用XFeat的特性对齐,匹配[18]和RANSAC的相似性转化[19]. 这些转变依次组成,将各科登记为共同坐标系统,中间部分作为参考. 评价部分组织图象也用于登记,以确保预测和地面真实基因表达剖面之间的准确空间对应,但被排除在模型培训、推论和性能评价之外。

blocks.en: Implementation Details and Evaluation Metrics. All experiments used PyTorch [ 20 ] with Adam [ 21 ] . Histology image features were extracted using the frozen UNI2-h [ 12 ] . The best model was selected based on validation performance, using 5% of ST spots randomly held out from each observed section. Hyperparameters were set to a learning rate of 10 − 3 10^{-3} , up to 1,000 epochs, a batch size of 512, latent dimensions d G = d I = 5 d_{G}=d_{I}=5 , and a loss weight λ = 1 \lambda=1 .

blocks.en: To evaluate reconstruction performance while minimizing slice-specific batch effects, we compute the Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) [ 9 ] between predicted and ground-truth expression across spatial locations for each gene within each section, then average across genes and sections. Following standard ST prediction protocols [ 22 ] , we evaluate the top 50 and 250 highly variable genes (HVGs) to mitigate measurement noise. We report mean performance over three random seeds.
blocks.zh: 为了评估重建性能,同时尽量减少切片特定批量效应,我们计算出皮尔逊相关系数(PCC)[9],即每个部分内每个基因在空间位置上的预测和地面真实表达,然后在基因和部分之间平均。 遵循标准的ST预测协议[22],我们评价前50和250个高度可变基因(HVGs)以减轻测量噪声. 我们报告三个随机种子的性能

blocks.en:
Comparisons. We compare our method with six baselines.
1) “NN” and 2) “KNN” interpolate gene expression from the nearest and k = 5 k=5 nearest observed spots, respectively.
3) “STAGE” [ 6 ] aligns autoencoder latent representations with spatial coordinates, enabling prediction at unobserved locations through its decoder.
4) “3D-STINR” [ 13 ] and 5) “3D-SUICA” [ 14 ] are INR-based methods originally developed for 2D ST and extended to 3D using spatially aligned coordinates across sections.
3D-STINR directly regresses gene expression from 3D coordinates, whereas 3D-SUICA first learns gene-expression embeddings using slice-wise graph autoencoders and then trains an INR to predict these embeddings from 3D coordinates, which are subsequently decoded into gene expression.
6) “SINTER3D” [ 7 ] predicts gene expression using an INR with additional intermediate-feature reconstruction losses to encourage spatial continuity.
blocks.zh:
比较. 我们把方法与六个基线相比较。
1)“NN”和2)“KNN”分别从最近的和k=5k=5的观测到的斑点内插基因表达。
3) “编码”[6]使自动编码器潜在表示与空间坐标相协调,从而能够通过其解码器对未观测到的地点进行预测。
4) “3D-STINR”[13]和5] “3D-SUICA”[14]是最初为2D ST开发的基于INR的方法,并使用跨段的空间坐标扩展为3D。
3D-STINR从3D坐标直接递归基因表达,而3D-SUICA首先使用切法图自动编码器学习基因表达嵌入,然后训练一个INR从3D坐标来预测这些嵌入,这些嵌入随后解码为基因表达.
6) “SINTER3D” [7] 预测基因表达时使用含有额外中间地貌重建损失的INR,以鼓励空间连续性。

blocks.en:
Table 1 presents the quantitative comparison.
Simple interpolation methods, NN and KNN, show poor performance.
STAGE performs well on HemiBrainA but shows limited performance on other datasets, indicating a lack of robustness across datasets. This may be because explicitly aligning gene-expression latent representations with spatial coordinates restricts their ability to capture complex expression patterns.
Similarly, 3D-STINR and SINTER3D show limited performance, potentially due to the difficulty of directly regressing high-dimensional expression vectors using INR.
In contrast, 3D-SUICA achieves relatively consistent performance, suggesting that low-dimensional latent modeling facilitates INR training.
Our method achieves the best performance on all metrics for 3DST-RA and HemiBrainB and on HVGs250 for HemiBrainA, demonstrating the effectiveness of histological supervision for continuous 3D reconstruction from sparse ST observations across datasets.
blocks.zh:
表1为定量比较。
简单的插值方法,NN和KNN,表现不佳.
STAGE在HemiBrain上表现良好 A但显示其他数据集的性能有限,表明数据集之间缺乏稳健性. 这可能是因为明确地将基因表达的潜在表示与空间坐标相配合限制了它们捕捉复杂表达模式的能力。
同样,3D-STINR和SINTER3D显示的性能有限,可能是由于使用INR直接递减高维度表达矢量的困难.
相比之下,3D-SUICA取得了相对一致的性能,表明低维潜在模型可以促进INR培训.
我们的方法在3DST-RA和HemiBrainB的所有度量衡上以及HVGs250对HemiBrainA的度量衡上都取得了最佳的性能,证明了组织学监督对连续的3D重建的有效性,这是通过对数据集的稀少ST观测.

blocks.en:
Ablation Study. To evaluate the effect of morphological supervision,
we compare our method with “Ours w/o HIM”,
which excludes image-based supervision.
Both reconstruct gene expression in the same
low-dimensional latent space, differing only in
whether the shared INR backbone receives additional
supervision from histological images.
As shown in Table 2 , our method achieves relatively consistent and competitive performance across datasets, suggesting that dense histological supervision helps the INR learn spatial continuity more reliably than gene expression alone.

我们把方法与“我们的w/o他”,

两者都以相同的方式重建基因表达

如表2所示,我们的方法实现了各数据集相对一致和竞争性的性能,这表明密集的组织学监督有助于国家自然资源研究所比仅基因表达更可靠地学习空间连续性。

blocks.en: To further assess histological supervision, we vary the number of missing ST sections (3, 5, and 7) on HemiBrainA, the largest dataset. The middle missing section is held out for evaluation, while the others provide only histological images. As shown in Fig. 2 , both methods perform comparably with three missing sections, whereas our method increasingly outperforms Ours w/o HIM as the number of missing sections increases. This suggests that histological supervision is particularly beneficial when sparse ST observations make learning spatial continuity from gene expression alone challenging.
blocks.zh: 为了进一步评估组织学监督,我们在HemiBrainA这个最大的数据集上对缺失的ST节(3,5和7)的数量有所变化. 中间缺失的部分被保留出来进行评价,而其他部分则只提供组织图象. 如图2所示,这两种方法与缺失的三段具有可比性,而随着缺失的三段数量增加,我们的方法正日益超过我们。 这表明,当很少的ST观测使仅基因表达的学习空间连续性成为挑战时,组织学监督就特别有益.

blocks.en:
Validity of Histology as Multi-task Supervision. To validate the use of densely sampled histological images as auxiliary supervision in multi-task learning, we consider an alternative that first interpolates histology image features at unobserved sections and then uses them as direct inputs to predict gene expression.
To evaluate this alternative without errors from histological feature interpolation, we train a linear probe on frozen UNI2-h features from ST-observed sections (UNI2-h+LP) and evaluate it using ground-truth histological images at the evaluation sections. Importantly, these images are unavailable in the actual reconstruction setting and are never provided to our method.
As shown in Table 3 , our method outperforms the
UNI2-h+LP baseline even when ground-truth histological
images are provided at the evaluation sections.
This suggests that histological supervision can be
beneficial for learning continuous spatial representations
beyond this simple image-based prediction strategy.
blocks.zh:
历史学作为多任务监督的有效性. 为了验证在多任务学习中将密集抽样的神学图像用作辅助监督,我们考虑一种替代方法,首先将神学图像特征插在未观测到的部分,然后将其作为直接输入来预测基因表达.
为了在不因组织特征内插而出现错误的情况下评价这一替代办法,我们从ST-observed段(UNI2-h+LP)对冷冻的UNI2-h特性进行线性探测,并在评价段使用地面-真实组织图像加以评价。 重要的是,这些图像在实际的重建环境中是不存在的,并且从未提供给我们的方法。

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en: We proposed HIM-INR, a histology-informed multi-task INR for continuous 3D gene-expression reconstruction from sparse ST observations. By jointly learning gene-expression and histological representations through a shared INR backbone, our method leverages densely sampled histological images as auxiliary supervision to capture spatial continuity between observed ST sections. Experiments on two 3D ST datasets demonstrated improved reconstruction over existing methods, with increasing benefits as ST observations become sparser. Importantly, our method enables gene-expression prediction at arbitrary 3D coordinates without requiring histological images at inference time.
blocks.zh: 我们提出HIM -INR, 一个神学上知情的多任务 INR,持续 3D基因表达重建 从稀少的ST观测。 通过通过共享的INR骨干,共同学习基因表达和神学表现,我们的方法利用了密集的神学图像样本作为辅助监督,捕捉观测到的ST各段之间的空间连续性. 对两个三维ST数据集的实验表明,重建工作比现有方法有所改善,随着ST观测越来越少,效益越来越大。 重要的是,我们的方法能够在任意的3D坐标上进行基因表达预测,而不需要推断时的组织图像。
